summary: NC.6 is planned as the frontier layer of the roadmap: the statements that connect the profinite and unipotent theory to rational points and that remain conjectural. On the profinite side it defines the conjugacy classes of Galois sections and the section map of rational points, proves (after Stix, Appendix B) that the section map is injective for curves of genus at least one over number fields by comparing sections of an abelian variety with its Kummer map, and states Grothendieck's section conjecture as a named proposition. On the unipotent side it states Kim's dimension conjecture (Kim 2009, Conjecture 1) and his Selmer-vanishing conjecture (Conjecture 2), plans the graded dimension formulas and the H² estimate they need, and plans every conditional bridge Kim gives (Selmer vanishing, Bloch–Kato, weight filtrations after Fontaine–Mazur, weak Jannsen, pseudo-nullity) together with the two known cases (the thrice-punctured line, after Kim 2005, and punctured CM elliptic curves of Selmer rank one). Finally it states Kim's eventual-equality conjecture of Balakrishnan–Dan-Cohen–Kim–Wewers with its S-integral variant and proves its depth-one instance for the thrice-punctured line. Every conjecture is a named proposition and every result that uses one lists it as a hypothesis. The export of NC.1–NC.5 outputs to EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.6 named in the stage text is process; restructure[0] proposes narrowing the stage to the frontier, superseding the earlier drop proposal. Eighteen nodes; twelve source findings in Kim 2009, BDCKW v4, Stix v1 and Kim 2005 v1, one of them rejected on review. Tangential base points in the unipotent theory are a recorded gap.

nodes.title: Conjugacy classes of Galois sections
nodes.statement: Let k be a field with separable closure k^s and Γ_k = Gal(k^s/k), and let X be a quasi-compact geometrically connected k-scheme with a geometric point x̄ of X_{k^s}. Write π = π_1^ét(X, x̄), Δ = π_1^ét(X_{k^s}, x̄) and pr: π → Γ_k for the projection of the arithmetic exact sequence 1 → Δ → π → Γ_k → 1 (IG.1). A section is a continuous group homomorphism s: Γ_k → π with pr ∘ s = id. The geometric kernel acts on sections by (δ·s)(σ) = δ s(σ) δ⁻¹. The set of sections modulo this action is Sect(X/k). Equivalently, π acts by γ·s = c_γ ∘ s ∘ c_{pr(γ)⁻¹} (conjugation c_γ), and this action has the same orbits, because π = Δ·s(Γ_k) and s(τ) acts trivially on s. A change of geometric base point along an étale path induces a bijection of the sets of classes that does not depend on the path, so Sect(X/k) depends only on X/k up to canonical bijection. When a reference section s_0 is fixed, s ↦ [σ ↦ s(σ) s_0(σ)⁻¹] identifies Sect(X/k) with the nonabelian H¹(Γ_k, Δ) of NC.3, where Γ_k acts on Δ by conjugation through s_0; the class of s_0 goes to the base point.
hypotheses: k any field; X quasi-compact and geometrically connected over k, so that the sequence of IG.1 is exact.
Sections are continuous homomorphisms of profinite groups; the equivalence relation is conjugation by the geometric kernel Δ only.
No hyperbolicity or properness is assumed in the definition; those hypotheses enter the theorems that use it.
proofSteps: Import the exact sequence 1 → Δ → π → Γ_k → 1 and its continuity from IG.1/arithmetic-exact-sequence.
Check that δ·s is again a continuous section (pr kills Δ) and that this is a group action; take orbits with Mathlib's orbit quotient.
Show that Kim's π-action has the same orbits: write γ = δ s(τ) and compute c_{s(τ)} ∘ s ∘ c_{τ⁻¹} = s.
Base-point change: an étale path p: x̄ → x̄' gives compatible isomorphisms of π and Δ (IG.0); a second path differs by an element of Δ, which acts trivially on classes.

With a reference section s_0, the difference σ ↦ s(σ)s_0(σ)⁻¹ is a continuous 1-cocycle for the s_0-twisted action, conjugation by δ changes it by the coboundary of δ, and every cocycle c gives the section c·s_0; this is the bijection with H¹(Γ_k, Δ) (NC.3/nonabelian-h1, NC.0/reference-section-change).
acceptance: For X = Spec k the kernel Δ is trivial, π = Γ_k, and Sect(Spec k/k) has exactly one element.
For X = P¹_k the kernel Δ is trivial (P¹ is simply connected over k^s), so Sect(P¹/k) is one point although P¹(k) is infinite when k is.
For X = G_{m,k} in characteristic zero Δ = Ẑ(1) and Sect(G_m/k) ≅ H¹(k, Ẑ(1)) ≅ lim_n k^×/k^{×n} by Kummer theory.

nodes.title: The section map of rational points
nodes.statement: For X/k as in section-classes and x ∈ X(k), the k-rational point gives a section s_x of π_1^ét(X, x̄_x) → Γ_k for a geometric point x̄_x over x (IG.1), whose image is a decomposition group of a point of the universal pro-étale cover over x. Transporting s_x along any étale path x̄_x → x̄ (NC.0/transferred-endpoint-section) gives a section of pr whose Δ-conjugacy class does not depend on the path. The section map is κ_X: X(k) → Sect(X/k), x ↦ [s_x]. If b ∈ X(k) is a reference point and Sect(X/k) is identified with H¹(Γ_k, Δ) through s_b, then κ_X(x) is the class of the Γ_k-equivariant Δ-torsor of étale paths from b to x (NC.0/arithmetic-geometric-paths). The map is natural for k-morphisms and compatible with restriction to finite separable extensions. κ_X(x) = κ_X(y) holds exactly when the path torsor P(x, y) has a Γ_k-fixed path (NC.0/path-section-comparison).
hypotheses: X quasi-compact and geometrically connected over k; x ∈ X(k).
The map uses only rational points. Tangential base points give cuspidal sections of open curves (IG.1/tame-tangential-fiber) that are not values of κ_X on X(k).
proofSteps: A k-point x: Spec k → X induces Γ_k = π_1(Spec k) → π_1(X, x̄_x), a section by functoriality (IG.1).
Transport along a path p: x̄_x → x̄ gives p s_x p⁻¹; replacing p by p·h with h ∈ Δ conjugates the result by h (NC.0/transferred-endpoint-section).
With reference b, the difference cocycle of the transported s_x against s_b is the cocycle of the path torsor P(b, x) (NC.0/arithmetic-path-cocycle).
Naturality follows from functoriality of path torsors and sections (NC.0/arithmetic-path-functoriality).
acceptance: For X = Spec k, κ_X is the unique map from a point to a point.
For X = P¹_k with k infinite, κ_X is constant and not injective.
For X = G_{m,k} with reference b = 1, κ_X(a) is the Kummer class of a ∈ k^×.

sources.match: Constructs the class of a splitting from a rational point by transporting the induced map on fundamental groups along an étale path, and notes the independence up to conjugacy.

nodes.title: Sections of an abelian variety and the Kummer map
nodes.statement: Let A/k be an abelian variety and n ≥ 1 invertible in k. Multiplication by n is a finite étale Galois cover A → A with group A[n](k^s); it defines a quotient π_1(A/k) → π^{[n]}(A/k), an extension of Γ_k by A[n](k^s). For a ∈ A(k), let s_a and s_0 be the images in π^{[n]}(A/k) of sections attached to a and to the origin. Then the difference cocycle σ ↦ s_a(σ) s_0(σ)⁻¹, with values in A[n](k^s), represents the Kummer class δ_n(a) ∈ H¹(k, A[n]) of RP.1/kummer-map, with the sign convention δ_n(a)(σ) = σ(b) − b for any b with nb = a. Passing to the limit over n, the image of κ_A(a) − κ_A(0) in H¹(k, T̂A), T̂A = lim_n A[n](k^s), is the profinite Kummer class of a. For a curve X with a rational point b and Jacobian J, combining with the Abel–Jacobi map ι_b and SF.3/tate-module-etale-h1, the abelianised section map of X is x ↦ Kummer class of [x − b].
hypotheses: A abelian variety over k; n invertible in k (all n when char k = 0).
Sign convention: Kummer cocycle σ(b) − b with nb = a, equal to the difference cocycle s_a s_0⁻¹.
proofSteps: Identify the fibre of [n]: A → A over 0 with A[n](k^s); s_0 acts on it through the natural Galois action.
To let s_a act on the fibre over 0, choose the path from 0 to a given on the cover [n] by translation by a fixed b with nb = a.
Compute s_a(σ)(P) = −b + σ(P + b) = σ(P) + (σ(b) − b), so s_a(σ)s_0(σ)⁻¹ is translation by σ(b) − b, a Kummer cocycle (RP.1/kummer-map).

Compatibility of the covers [nm] → [n] gives the inverse limit statement; for Jacobians use the Abel–Jacobi functoriality of sections and the identification of T̂J with the abelianised geometric fundamental group (SF.3/tate-module-etale-h1).
acceptance: For E: y² = x³ − x over Q and a = (0, 0), δ_2(a) ≠ 0 because E(Q) = E[2](Q) ≅ (Z/2)² and so 2E(Q) = 0; hence the images of s_a and s_0 in π^{[2]}(E/Q) are not conjugate.
For a = 0 the difference cocycle is trivial and δ_n(0) = 0.

nodes.title: Injectivity of the section map
nodes.statement: Let k be a field such that, for every abelian variety A/k, the group A(k) has no nonzero element divisible by every n ≥ 1 invertible in k. If X/k is a geometrically connected variety that admits an immersion into an abelian variety over k, then κ_X: X(k) → Sect(X/k) is injective. Consequently, for a number field k and a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X/k of genus g ≥ 1 (in particular for every proper hyperbolic curve, g ≥ 2), the section map κ_X is injective.
hypotheses: The divisibility hypothesis concerns all abelian varieties over k; over a number field it follows from the Mordell–Weil theorem.
For a curve, X(k) = ∅ makes the statement empty; otherwise a rational point b gives the Abel–Jacobi closed immersion X → J for g ≥ 1.
The theorem is stated for every field satisfying the divisibility hypothesis; its number-field instance is derived here from Mordell–Weil.
proofSteps: If X(k) is empty there is nothing to prove; otherwise fix an immersion ι: X → A over k (for a curve, the Abel–Jacobi map at b, RP.6/curve-in-jacobian).
By naturality of the section map (sectionClassMap_natural) it suffices to show injectivity for A, since ι is injective on k-points.
If κ_A(x) = κ_A(y), then for every n the images in π^{[n]}(A/k) are conjugate, so by NC.6/kummer-section-comparison δ_n(x − y) = 0, that is x − y ∈ nA(k) for all n.

By hypothesis x − y = 0. Over a number field A(k) is finitely generated (RP.1/mordell-weil), and a finitely generated abelian group has no nonzero element divisible by every n: write it as Z^r ⊕ (finite) and take n a multiple of the torsion exponent.
acceptance: Elliptic curves over Q: for E: y² = x³ − x, the four rational points have pairwise distinct section classes.
The non-example P¹_Q (no immersion into an abelian variety, κ constant) shows the immersion hypothesis cannot be dropped.
The elementary step: in Z ⊕ Z/6, an element divisible by every n ≥ 1 is zero.

States the section conjecture whose injective half this node proves.

nodes.title: Grothendieck's section conjecture
nodes.statement: For a field k and a quasi-compact geometrically connected k-scheme X, the proposition SectionConjecture(X/k) states that the section map κ_X: X(k) → Sect(X/k) is a bijection. Grothendieck's section conjecture is the proposition that SectionConjecture(X/k) holds for every number field k and every smooth projective geometrically connected curve X/k of genus at least 2. It is an open problem: it is stated as a named proposition, and any result that uses it lists it among its hypotheses. By NC.6/section-map-injective, for such X it is equivalent to surjectivity of κ_X; in particular it predicts that a curve without rational points has no sections. The cuspidal form for affine hyperbolic curves, the birational form and the p-adic forms are different statements and are not this definition.
hypotheses: The proposition is about rational points and conjugacy classes of continuous sections; it is not asserted.
The genus bound and the number-field hypothesis are part of the conjecture, not of the proposition SectionConjecture(X/k).
proofSteps: Define SectionConjecture(X/k) as bijectivity of κ_X (section-class-map).
Define the global conjecture by quantifying over number fields and smooth projective geometrically connected curves of genus ≥ 2.
Derive the equivalence with surjectivity from NC.6/section-map-injective.
acceptance: SectionConjecture(Spec k/k) holds for every field k.
SectionConjecture(P¹_Q/Q) and SectionConjecture(G_{m,Q}/Q) both fail, for different reasons (non-injective, non-surjective).

sources.match: Formulates the section conjecture for smooth compact hyperbolic curves over number fields as bijectivity of the map from rational points to conjugacy classes of splittings, citing Grothendieck's 1983 letter.

Restates the conjecture in the H¹ form and compares its surjectivity with the surjectivity statement for Selmer schemes.

nodes.title: Kim's dimension conjecture
nodes.statement: Setting (Kim 2009, pp.91–96): X is a smooth hyperbolic curve over Q, 𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳′ a smooth model over Z[1/S] with smooth compactification and smooth complement, b ∈ 𝒳(Z[1/S]) or an integral tangential base point (for a tangential base point the unipotent group, Selmer variety and Albanese map are those of NC.2–NC.4 at the tangential fibre functor, which is a recorded gap of this layer), p ∉ S a prime of good reduction and T = S ∪ {p}. Depth n means the quotient U⟨n⟩ = U/Γ_{n+1}U of the Q_p-unipotent étale fundamental group U of X_{Q̄} at b (NC.2), which is Kim's U_{n+1}; S_n = H¹_f(G_T, U⟨n⟩) is the Selmer variety (classes crystalline at p, no condition at the other places of T), an affine Q_p-scheme of finite type (NC.3), and Q_n = U_dR⟨n⟩/F⁰ is the target of the depth-n de Rham Albanese map at p (NC.4). The proposition KimDimensionConjecture(X, p) states: there is n ≥ 1 with dim S_n < dim Q_n (Kim 2009, Conjecture 1). By NC.4/dimension-finiteness the inequality at one depth n gives finiteness of 𝒳(Z[1/S]), and of X(Q) when X is proper. The conjecture is open for curves of positive genus; it is stated as a named proposition, and every result that uses it lists it as a hypothesis. Refining the local conditions (for example the stringent conditions of BDCKW or the potentially unramified conditions of Kim §4) replaces S_n by a closed subscheme and can only lower dim S_n.
hypotheses: X hyperbolic over Q (2g − 2 + s > 0 where s is the number of geometric points of the boundary); p ∉ S of good reduction for 𝒳′ and the boundary.
Dimensions are Krull dimensions of the represented affine schemes; dim Q_n = dim U_dR⟨n⟩ − dim F⁰U_dR⟨n⟩.
Depth indexing follows NC.2/NC.4 (depth 1 is the abelian quotient).
An integral tangential base point uses the recorded gap on tangential base points; an S-integral base point uses NC.2–NC.4 as they stand.
proofSteps: Take S_n from NC.3/selmer-functor and NC.3/finite-level-representability with only the crystalline condition at p.
Take Q_n and the de Rham Albanese map from NC.4/local-albanese.
Define the proposition as the existence of a depth with the strict inequality.

If b is tangential and 𝒳(Z[1/S]) is nonempty, change to an S-integral base point by kimDimensionConjecture_basepoint (twisting by the path torsor, BDCKW §2.9), which preserves dim S_n and dim Q_n; if 𝒳(Z[1/S]) is empty the finiteness statement is empty.
Prove finite_of_kimDimensionConjecture from NC.4/dimension-finiteness at that depth (with NC.4/rational-integral-containment).
acceptance: At depth 1 for a proper curve of genus g whose Jacobian has p-adic Selmer rank r, the inequality is r < g, Chabauty's condition (NC.4/depth-one-locus).
For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z the inequality already holds at depth 1 (0 < 2).

sources.match: States the conjectural dimension inequality for some depth over Q, explains that it yields finiteness as in Chabauty's argument, and records that it is known in genus zero and some genus-one cases.

uses.how: The dimension inequality at one depth gives a nonzero algebraic function vanishing on the Selmer image, hence finiteness.
Conclusion of the conditional bridges from motivic conjectures.
The known cases of the inequality.
Finiteness of X(Z_p)_n as soon as the localisation image is a proper subvariety.

api.name: KimDimensionConjecture
api.statement: The proposition ∃ n ≥ 1, dim S_n < dim Q_n for the data (X, 𝒳, b, p, S).

api.name: finite_of_kimDimensionConjecture
api.statement: KimDimensionConjecture(X, p) implies that 𝒳(Z[1/S]) is finite, and that X(Q) is finite if X is proper.

api.name: kimDimensionConjecture_of_refined
api.statement: If S′_n ⊆ S_n is the Selmer variety for finer local conditions, dim S′_n ≤ dim S_n; the inequality for S_n implies it for S′_n, and finiteness follows from either (NC.4/locus-compatibilities).

api.name: kimDimensionConjecture_basepoint
api.statement: The proposition does not depend on the integral base point b: change of base point gives isomorphic Selmer varieties (BDCKW §2.9) and the de Rham dimensions are independent of b.

api.name: dim_Q_eq_sum
api.statement: dim Q_n = Σ_{k=1}^{n} (d_k − f_k), where d_k = dim gr_k U and f_k = dim F⁰ gr_k U_dR (NC.6/graded-central-dimensions).

api.name: KimDimensionInequality
api.statement: The form on dimension sequences: for selDim, dRDim : ℕ → ℕ, ∃ n ≥ 1, selDim n < dRDim n; KimDimensionConjecture is the instance selDim n = dim S_n, dRDim n = dim Q_n.

api.name: kimDimensionInequality_mono

tests.name: kimDimensionConjecture_depth_one_chabauty
tests.statement: For a proper curve of genus g over Q whose Jacobian has p-adic Bloch–Kato Selmer rank r, the depth-1 inequality dim S_1 < dim Q_1 is the classical condition r < g.

tests.name: kimDimensionConjecture_thrice_punctured_Z
tests.statement: For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z (S = ∅): dim S_1 = 0 (H¹_f(G_T, Q_p(1)) = Z^× ⊗ Q_p = 0) and dim Q_1 = 2, so the inequality holds at n = 1.

tests.name: kimDimensionConjecture_thrice_punctured_half
tests.statement: For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z[1/2]: dim S_1 = 2 = dim Q_1, so depth 1 fails, while dim S_2 = 2 < 3 = dim Q_2 (H¹(G_T, Q_p(2)) = 0); the inequality first holds at depth 2.

tests.name: not_kimDimensionConjecture_gm
tests.statement: For the non-hyperbolic G_m over Z[1/2], U = Q_p(1) is abelian, U⟨n⟩ = U⟨1⟩, and dim S_n = 1 = dim Q_n for every n, so the inequality never holds, matching the infinitude of G_m(Z[1/2]) = ±2^Z.

tests.name: kimDimensionConjecture_needs_crystalline
tests.statement: Dropping the crystalline condition at p is wrong: for P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z, H¹(G_T, Q_p(1)) = Z[1/p]^× ⊗ Q_p is one-dimensional, so the unconditioned depth-1 variety has dimension 2 = dim Q_1.

nodes.title: Dimensions of the lower central quotients
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth curve over a number field with smooth compactification of genus g and s ≥ 0 boundary points over the algebraic closure, hyperbolic (2g − 2 + s > 0), and let d_n = dim gr_n U, where gr_n U = Γ_nU/Γ_{n+1}U for the Q_p-unipotent étale (or de Rham) fundamental group U of NC.2. If s ≥ 1, U is the unipotent completion of a free group on m = 2g + s − 1 generators and Σ_{k | n} k·d_k = m^n (Witt), so d_n = (1/n) Σ_{k | n} μ(k) m^{n/k}. If s = 0 (so g ≥ 2), U is the completion of a surface group with one relation of degree 2 and Σ_{k | n} k·d_k = α^n + β^n with α, β = g ± √(g² − 1) (Labute), so d_n = (1/n) Σ_{k | n} μ(k)(α^{n/k} + β^{n/k}). In both cases gr_1 U = H₁ has dimension m (resp. 2g), gr_n U is a G_T-equivariant quotient of H₁^{⊗n}, and d_n ~ λ^n/n with λ = m (resp. α); in the hyperbolic case λ > g.
hypotheses: Hyperbolic smooth curve; the dimensions are those of the graded pieces of the lower central series of the Q_p-unipotent completion, equal to the ranks of the graded pieces of the discrete group.
gr_n is taken with Γ_1U = U, so gr_1 U is the abelianisation H₁.
proofSteps: The topological fundamental group of the complex points is free on m generators (s ≥ 1) or the one-relator surface group (s = 0); the unipotent completion has the same graded Lie algebra tensored with Q_p (NC.2/etale-galois, NC.2/central-quotients).
Free case: the graded Lie algebra is free on H₁, and Witt's formula (QM.6/free-lie-algebra-character-formula) gives d_n.

Surface case: the graded Lie algebra is the free Lie algebra on 2g generators modulo the ideal generated by the symplectic element of degree 2; its enveloping algebra has Hilbert series 1/(1 − 2g t + t²), which gives the stated divisor sum (Labute).
gr_n is spanned by iterated brackets of degree-1 elements, so it is a quotient of H₁^{⊗n}; the asymptotics follow from the divisor sums.
acceptance: g = 1, s = 0 (not hyperbolic): the formula gives d_1 = 2 and d_n = 0 for n ≥ 2, the abelian case.

sources.match: States the two recursive divisor-sum formulas for the graded dimensions, citing Labute for the surface-group case, and their asymptotics.

sources.locator: §1.7.6 (lower central series and parafree groups), equation (32), p.62
sources.match: Reports Labute's theorem that the graded Lie algebra of a one-relator group whose relator is not a proper power modulo the lower central series is a one-relator Lie algebra, gives the closed Möbius formula for the ranks in genus 2, and the exponential growth rate g + √(g² − 1) in genus g; expanding its inner sum as α^d + β^d with α + β = 4, αβ = 1 recovers Kim's divisor sum.

nodes.title: Vanishing of the strict Selmer groups of tensor powers
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, X/F a smooth curve, p a prime and T a finite set of places of F containing the places above p, the archimedean places and the places of bad reduction of X and its boundary. Put V_n = H¹_ét(X_{F̄}, Q_p)^{⊗n}(1), a continuous Q_p-representation of G_T. For a finite-dimensional continuous representation V of G_T, Sel⁰_T(V) is the kernel of H¹(G_T, V) → ⊕_{w ∈ T} H¹(G_w, V), the group Ш¹_T(V) with rational coefficients. The proposition SelmerVanishing(X, p, T) states that Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0 for all sufficiently large n (Kim 2009, Conjecture 2). It is open in general and is stated as a named proposition.
hypotheses: Continuous cohomology of the profinite group G_T with Q_p-coefficients (limits of lattices, as in ArithmeticGaloisDuality).
The local maps are restrictions to decomposition groups G_w for w ∈ T; no condition is imposed outside T beyond being unramified there.
proofSteps: Define V_n from H¹ of the curve with the G_T action (SF.3/tate-module-etale-h1 for the proper part; NC.2 for the unipotent comparison).
Define Sel⁰_T(V) as the kernel of localisation, Ш¹_T(V) of AGD R02.4/restricted-product-cohomology, extended to rational coefficients by R02.4/lattice-rational-poitou-tate.
Define the proposition by an eventually-true statement in n.
acceptance: For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Q, V_n ≅ Q_p(1 − n)^{2^n} and Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0 for n ≥ 2.
For n = 1 and a proper curve, V_1 ≅ V_pJ by the Weil pairing and Sel⁰_T(V_pJ) is the fine Selmer space of J.

sources.locator: §3, Conjecture 2 and the definition of Sel⁰_T before it, p.121
sources.match: Defines the strict Selmer group as the kernel of localisation at T and conjectures its vanishing on the twisted tensor powers of H¹ for large n.

uses.how: Through Poitou–Tate duality it bounds H² of the graded pieces, which forces the dimension inequality.
Bloch–Kato and a weight-filtration form of Fontaine–Mazur each imply it.
Hypothesis of the H² estimate and of the implication to Conjecture 1.

api.name: SelmerVanishing
api.statement: The proposition: Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0 for all sufficiently large n.

api.name: sel0_eq_sha1
api.statement: Sel⁰_T(V) is Ш¹_T(V) of ArithmeticGaloisDuality with rational coefficients.

api.name: sel0_dual_sha2
api.statement: Poitou–Tate: Sel⁰_T(V) is dual to Ш²_T(V^∨(1)); for V = V_n, V^∨(1) = H₁^{⊗n} with H₁ = H¹(X_{F̄}, Q_p)^∨, so SelmerVanishing is equivalent to Ш²_T(H₁^{⊗n}) = 0 for n ≫ 0.

api.name: sel0_mono_T
api.statement: For T ⊆ T′, inflation identifies Sel⁰_{T′}(V) with a subspace of Sel⁰_T(V).

api.name: selmerVanishing_of_finite_extension
api.statement: If F′/F is finite, SelmerVanishing over F′ implies it over F, since restriction is injective on H¹ with Q_p-coefficients.

api.name: EventuallyVanishing
api.statement: The form on dimension sequences: dim n = 0 for all large n; SelmerVanishing is the instance dim n = dim Sel⁰_T(V_n).

tests.name: selmerVanishing_thrice_punctured
tests.statement: For X = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Q, Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0 for every n ≥ 2: V_n ≅ Q_p(1 − n)^{2^n}, Ш¹_T(Q_p(j)) is dual to Ш²_T(Q_p(1 − j)), and H²(G_T, Q_p(m)) = 0 for m ≥ 2 (Soulé).

tests.name: sel0_eq_sha1_test
tests.statement: For any V, Sel⁰_T(V) equals the kernel of the localisation map of AGD R02.4/restricted-product-cohomology after tensoring with Q_p.

tests.name: selmerVanishing_needs_local_conditions
tests.statement: Dropping the local conditions is wrong: for X = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Q and every even n ≥ 2, V_n ≅ Q_p(1 − n)^{2^n} with 1 − n odd, so complex conjugation acts on it by −1 and Tate's global Euler characteristic formula gives dim H¹(G_T, Q_p(1 − n)) ≥ 1. The unrestricted H¹(G_T, V_n) is therefore nonzero for infinitely many n, while Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0 for every n ≥ 2 (selmerVanishing_thrice_punctured).

tests.name: selmerVanishing_zero_rep
tests.statement: For V = 0, Sel⁰_T(V) = 0.

nodes.title: Kim's H² estimate
nodes.statement: Assume SelmerVanishing(X, p, T) for X/F as in selmer-vanishing-conjecture, with compactification of genus g and s boundary points. Then there is an explicit polynomial P, depending only on g, s and |T|, such that dim_{Q_p} H²(G_T, gr_n U) ≤ P(n)·g^n for all sufficiently large n (with g^n read as 0 when g = 0 and n ≥ 2, where the local invariants vanish). At a place w ∤ p the local contribution is at most n·dim Gr^W_2·g^{n−1} + (n(n−1)/2)(dim Gr^W_1)²·g^{n−2} from the weight filtration of H¹ attached to semistable reduction, plus the boundary contribution n(s − 1)g^{n−1}; at w | p it is at most n(g + s − 1)g^{n−1}, from the Hodge–Tate weights of H¹.
hypotheses: SelmerVanishing(X, p, T) holds; n is beyond the threshold it provides.
gr_n U is the G_T-equivariant quotient of H₁^{⊗n} of NC.6/graded-central-dimensions, H₁ = H¹(X_{F̄}, Q_p)^∨.
proofSteps: H² is right exact on Q_p-representations of G_T: for finite p-primary M, H³(G_T, M) ≅ ⊕_{v real} H³(G_v, M) is killed by 2 (AGD R02.4/cohomological-dimension-bound; cd_p(G_T) = 2 when p is odd or F is totally imaginary), so after passing to lattices and inverting p (R02.4/lattice-rational-poitou-tate) H³ vanishes with Q_p-coefficients for every p, including p = 2 when F has a real place. Hence H²(G_T, H₁^{⊗n}) ↠ H²(G_T, gr_n U).
By SelmerVanishing and Poitou–Tate (sel0_dual_sha2), Ш²_T(H₁^{⊗n}) = 0, so H²(G_T, H₁^{⊗n}) injects into ⊕_{w ∈ T} H²(G_w, H₁^{⊗n}).
Local duality (AGD D7/local-coefficient-field-duality): dim H²(G_w, H₁^{⊗n}) = dim H⁰(G_w, H¹^{⊗n}(1)).

For w ∤ p: by the Gysin sequence (EDC.3, requested) H¹(X_{F̄}) is an extension of the boundary part ker(Q_p(−1)^{D(F̄)} → Q_p(−1)), which is Q_p(−1)^{s−1} after a finite extension making the boundary points rational (invariants only grow), by H¹ of the compactification X′; the invariants of H¹^{⊗n}(1) are bounded by the sum of those of the induced graded pieces. On H¹(X′), after a finite extension giving semistable reduction, the weight filtration W_0 ⊂ W_1 ⊂ W_2 has dim W_0 = dim Gr_2 ≤ g (DWP.10). Invariants come only from weight-zero tensors: one factor of weight 2 (from Gr_2 of H¹(X′) or from the boundary) and n − 1 of weight 0, or two factors of weight 1 and n − 2 of weight 0, which gives the stated count (Kim describes the filtration on H¹(X̄) without the boundary term: source issue E-NC6-kim-lemma6-open).

For w | p: with the convention HT(χ) = +1 of R06.2, H¹(X′_{F̄}) is de Rham with Hodge–Tate decomposition (H¹(X′, O) ⊗ C_p) ⊕ (H⁰(X′, Ω¹) ⊗ C_p(−1)) (R06.5 for the proper curve X′, R06.2 de Rham ⇒ Hodge–Tate), and the boundary part is C_p(−1)^{s−1}; together this is Kim's decomposition (H¹(X′, O) ⊗ C_p) ⊕ (H⁰(X′, Ω¹(log D)) ⊗ C_p(−1)), of dimensions g and g + s − 1. On each graded piece of H¹^{⊗n}(1) the invariants embed in the weight-zero part (Tate, R06.2), which needs exactly one factor from the C_p(−1) part, giving n(g + s − 1)g^{n−1}.
acceptance: For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} (g = 0) the bound gives H²(G_T, gr_n U) = 0 for n ≥ 2, consistent with Soulé's vanishing H²(G_T, Q_p(n)) = 0.
For g ≥ 2 the bound grows like n²g^n, slower than d_n ~ α^n/n since α = g + √(g² − 1) > g.

sources.match: Bounds H² of the graded pieces by a polynomial times g^n, using the surjection from H² of the tensor power of H₁, Conjecture 2 with Poitou–Tate, local duality, the weight filtration from Raynaud's uniformisation away from p and the Hodge–Tate decomposition at p. The weight filtration is described for H¹ of the compactification, and the boundary term for affine curves is added here (source issue E-NC6-kim-lemma6-open); the cohomological-dimension remark needs its rational-coefficient form at p = 2 (E-NC6-kim-cd2-p2).

nodes.title: Selmer vanishing implies the dimension conjecture
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth hyperbolic curve over Q with the data of kim-dimension-conjecture. If SelmerVanishing(X, p, T) holds, then KimDimensionConjecture(X, p) holds; hence 𝒳(Z[1/S]) is finite (and X(Q) if X is proper). Precisely, for n large (of suitable parity), dim S_n ≤ Σ_{k ≤ n} dim H¹(G_T, gr_k U) ≤ Σ_{k ≤ n} (d_k⁻ + P(k)g^k) < Σ_{k ≤ n} (d_k − g^k) ≤ dim Q_n, where d_k⁻ is the dimension of the (−1)-eigenspace of complex conjugation on gr_k U. Here d_k⁻ = (d_k − τ_k)/2 with τ_k the trace of complex conjugation, computed from its trace t on H₁. In the proper case τ_k = 0 for odd k (gr_k U is pure of odd weight −k). In the affine case τ_k = (1/k) Σ_{e | k} μ(e) t_e^{k/e} with t_e = t for odd e and t_e = m for even e; either |t| < m, and then |τ_k| = o(d_k), or t = −m (genus 0 with all boundary points real), and then complex conjugation acts on gr_k U by (−1)^k. In every case Σ_{k ≤ n} d_k⁺ ≥ c·λ^n/n for infinitely many n, with λ > g.
hypotheses: SelmerVanishing(X, p, T); X hyperbolic over Q; T = S ∪ {p} with p of good reduction.
The comparison of eigenspace dimensions uses the corrected count of source issue E-NC6-kim-conjugation-eigenspaces, not Kim's printed value d_k/2.
proofSteps: The central extensions 1 → gr_{n}U → U⟨n⟩ → U⟨n−1⟩ → 1 make H¹(G_T, U⟨n⟩) fibred over a subvariety of H¹(G_T, U⟨n−1⟩) with fibres torsors under H¹(G_T, gr_n U) (NC.3/central-extension, NC.3/finite-level-representability), so dim S_n ≤ Σ_{k ≤ n} dim H¹(G_T, gr_k U).

H⁰(G_T, gr_k U) = 0 for k ≥ 1 (weights of H₁ are −1 and −2), so Tate's global Euler characteristic formula over Q (AGD R02.4/global-euler-characteristic with rational coefficients) gives dim H¹ − dim H² = d_k⁻.
Bound dim H² by NC.6/h2-growth-bound and dim F⁰ gr_k U_dR by g^k (F⁰ of H₁^{dR ⊗k} has dimension dim H¹(O)^{⊗k} = g^k), so dim Q_n ≥ Σ_{k ≤ n} (d_k − g^k).

Trace of complex conjugation c: in the affine case gr_• U is the free Lie algebra on H₁ with c acting through H₁, so τ_k is given by the graded character formula of free Lie algebras applied to the involution c (QM.6/free-lie-algebra-character-formula). On H₁, c has trace 0 on the compact part (it is antisymplectic) and trace 1 − r on the boundary part of the Gysin sequence (EDC.3, requested), r being the number of real boundary points; hence t = 1 − r, and t = −m exactly when g = 0 and every boundary point is real. In the proper case τ_k = 0 for odd k because gr_k U is pure of odd weight −k.

Compare: the difference is at least Σ_{k ≤ n} d_k⁺ − Σ_{k ≤ n} (P(k) + 1)g^k, and by NC.6/graded-central-dimensions and the trace computation Σ_{k ≤ n} d_k⁺ ≥ c·λ^n/n for infinitely many n with λ > g; choose such n.
Finiteness then follows from finite_of_kimDimensionConjecture.
acceptance: For a proper curve of genus 2, λ = 2 + √3 ≈ 3.73 > 2 = g, and the counting step succeeds once Σ_{k ≤ n} d_k/2 over odd k exceeds Σ_{k ≤ n} (P(k) + 1)2^k.
For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} complex conjugation acts on gr_k U ≅ Q_p(k)^{d_k} by (−1)^k, so d_k⁺ = d_k for even k and 0 for odd k; the count succeeds through the even degrees.

sources.match: Proves that Conjecture 2 implies Conjecture 1 by comparing the growth of the graded dimensions with the Euler characteristic and the H² estimate; the eigenspace value printed on p.123 needs the correction recorded in sourceIssues.

nodes.title: Bloch–Kato implies Selmer vanishing
nodes.statement: Let X/F be a smooth curve over a number field and p, T as in selmer-vanishing-conjecture. Suppose that, for every n ≥ 2, the group H¹_g(G_F, H^n(X^n_{F̄}, Q_p(1))) of classes unramified at almost all places and de Rham (potentially semistable) at the places above p is spanned by the image of K-theory under the étale Chern class map, as predicted by the Bloch–Kato conjecture (their Conjecture 5.3, as cited by Kim). Since the relevant K-group K^{(1)}_{1−n}(X^n) is zero for n ≥ 2, this hypothesis says that H¹_g(G_F, H^n(X^n_{F̄}, Q_p(1))) = 0 for n ≥ 2. Then SelmerVanishing(X, p, T) holds; in fact Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0 for every n ≥ 2.
hypotheses: The Bloch–Kato fragment for the motives h^n(X^n)(1), n ≥ 2, is a hypothesis; it is not a theorem of any roadmap.
For open X the smooth variety X^n is not proper and the hypothesis is the corresponding statement for its cohomology.
proofSteps: By Künneth, V_n = H¹(X_{F̄}, Q_p)^{⊗n}(1) is a G_F-stable direct summand of H^n(X^n_{F̄}, Q_p(1)).
A class in Sel⁰_T(V_n) is unramified outside T and locally trivial at T, so it lies in H¹_g(G_F, V_n) ⊆ H¹_g(G_F, H^n(X^n_{F̄}, Q_p(1))) (PHR L1/bloch-kato-subgroups).
The weight-graded piece K^{(1)}_{2r−n−1} with r = 1 is a negative K-group of the regular scheme X^n for n ≥ 2, hence zero, so the hypothesis gives H¹_g = 0 and therefore Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0.
acceptance: For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Q the conclusion holds unconditionally (selmerVanishing_thrice_punctured), consistent with Soulé's theorem.
The hypothesis is used only through the vanishing of H¹_g; no regulator computation enters.

sources.locator: §3, Observation 1 and the paragraph before it, pp.121–122
sources.match: Places Sel⁰_T(V_n) inside H¹_g of a twisted cohomology group of X^n and deduces Conjecture 2 from Bloch–Kato's conjectured isomorphism with K-theory, whose source group vanishes in this range.

nodes.title: Weight filtrations on extensions imply Selmer vanishing
nodes.statement: Let X/F and V_n be as in selmer-vanishing-conjecture and n ≥ 3. Suppose every extension 0 → V_n → E → Q_p → 0 of G_T-representations whose class lies in Sel⁰_T(V_n) carries a finite increasing filtration W by G_T-subrepresentations, strictly compatible with the maps of the extension, inducing on Q_p the filtration pure of weight 0 and on V_n a filtration with W_0V_n = 0. Then Sel⁰_T(V_n) = 0. The hypothesis is what Kim (following Scholl) derives from the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture together with the expectation that such extensions are Q_p-linear combinations of extensions of geometric origin; it is a stated hypothesis here. For proper X, V_n is pure of weight n − 2 and W_0V_n = 0 for n ≥ 3; for open X the weights of V_n lie in [n − 2, 2n − 2] and the same conclusion holds.
hypotheses: The weight-filtration hypothesis on each extension class in Sel⁰_T(V_n); n ≥ 3.
Weights of V_n come from the weights 1 (compact part) and 2 (boundary part) of H¹ at good places.
proofSteps: Strictness gives v ∈ W_0E mapping to 1 ∈ Q_p.

W_0E ∩ V_n = W_0V_n = 0 since all weights of V_n are at least n − 2 ≥ 1: at good places H¹ of the compactification is pure of weight 1 (WEC R34.2) and the boundary part of the Gysin sequence (EDC.3, requested) has weight 2.
Hence W_0E is a one-dimensional G_T-stable complement of V_n, the extension splits and its class is zero.
acceptance: For n = 2 and proper X, V_2 has weight 0 and the argument does not apply.
For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}, V_n = Q_p(1 − n)^{2^n} has weight 2n − 2 ≥ 4 for n ≥ 3.

sources.locator: §3, Observation 2 and the argument after it, p.122
sources.match: Attributes to Scholl the deduction of Conjecture 2 from the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture via weight filtrations on geometric extensions, and splits the extension through its weight-zero part for n ≥ 3; the purity claim needs the open-curve correction recorded in sourceIssues.

nodes.title: Weak Jannsen vanishing implies the dimension conjecture for affine curves
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth affine hyperbolic curve over Q (s ≥ 1) with compactification X′ of genus g and the data of kim-dimension-conjecture. Assume the weak Jannsen conjecture: there is k > 0 such that H²(G_T, H^i(V_{Q̄}, Q_p)(r)) = 0 for every smooth projective V/Q with good reduction outside T, every i and every r ≥ i + k. Then KimDimensionConjecture(X, p) holds, so 𝒳(Z[1/S]) is finite.
hypotheses: X affine (s ≥ 1); the weak Jannsen vanishing is a hypothesis for all smooth projective V/Q with good reduction outside T.
Kim records that the argument was not adapted to the compact case.
proofSteps: Pass to the finite extension F′ over which all boundary points are rational; F′/Q is unramified outside T, and corestriction makes the H² estimate over F′ suffice. The hypothesis over Q gives it over F′: for V′/F′ smooth projective with good reduction outside T, Shapiro's lemma identifies H²(G_{F′,T}, H^i(V′)(r)) with H²(G_{Q,T}, Ind H^i(V′)(r)), and Ind H^i(V′) is a direct summand of H^i of the Weil restriction Res_{F′/Q}V′ (Künneth, EDC.0), which is smooth projective with good reduction outside T.
Use the dual Gysin sequence 0 → Q_p(1)^{s−1} → H₁(X) → H₁(X′) → 0 (EDC.3, requested) and, in the Grothendieck group, expand H₁(X)^{⊗n} into tensor products of V = H₁(X′) ≅ H¹(X′)(1) and Q_p(1).
V^{⊗l} is a direct summand of H^l(X′^l_{Q̄})(l) (Künneth), so H²(G_T, V^{⊗l}(r)) = 0 for r ≥ k by the hypothesis.

For g ≥ 1: the Weil pairing embeds Q_p(1) in V^{⊗2} as a direct summand; writing V^{⊗2k} = M ⊕ Q_p(k) and iterating, dim H²(G_T, V^{⊗n}(l)) ≤ C·a^n with a = ((2g)^{2k} − 1)^{1/(2k)} < 2g ≤ m. For g = 0, V = 0 and H₁(X)^{⊗n} = Q_p(n)^{(s−1)^n}, and H²(G_T, Q_p(n)) = 0 for n ≥ k is the hypothesis for V = Spec Q (i = 0), so the bound holds with 0 for n ≥ k.
Combine with the Euler characteristic and the graded dimensions d_n ~ m^n/n as in vanishing-implies-dimension.
acceptance: For g = 0 every tensor power of H₁ is a sum of Tate twists and the hypothesis reduces to Soulé's vanishing of H²(G_T, Q_p(r)) for r ≥ 2.
The bound C·a^n with a < m is the only input from the hypothesis.

sources.locator: §3, statement of the weak Jannsen conjecture, Observation 3 and its proof, pp.125–126
sources.match: Shows for affine curves that a uniform vanishing of H² in large twists bounds H² of the tensor powers by an exponential of base below m, which suffices for Conjecture 1.

nodes.title: Integral points on punctured CM elliptic curves of rank one
nodes.statement: Let E/Q be an elliptic curve with complex multiplication, X = E ∖ {O} with its minimal model 𝒳 and an integral base point b ∈ 𝒳(Z) (if 𝒳(Z) is empty there is nothing to prove), p an odd prime of good reduction and T the bad primes together with p. Assume that the Bloch–Kato Selmer group H¹_f(G_Q, V_pE) has dimension one (this holds, for example, when E(Q) has rank one and Ш(E)[p^∞] is finite). Let Sel_T(U⟨n⟩) be the refined Selmer variety of classes potentially unramified at the primes of T other than p and potentially crystalline at p. Then dim Sel_T(U⟨2⟩) ≤ 1 < 2 = dim U_dR⟨2⟩/F⁰, so the integral points 𝒳(Z) form a finite set, without any conjectural input.
hypotheses: CM ensures potentially good reduction everywhere (good reduction over Q(E[12])), which defines the potentially unramified conditions.
Selmer rank one is a hypothesis on V_pE; rank E(Q) = 1 alone does not give it without finiteness of Ш(E)[p^∞] (source issue E-NC6-kim-rank-one).
The base point is integral, as NC.2–NC.4 require; Kim §4 does not fix one, and the finiteness statement is empty when 𝒳(Z) = ∅.
proofSteps: Depth-two graded piece: gr_2 U = Λ²H₁ ≅ Q_p(1) (NC.6/graded-central-dimensions with m = 2).
The refined central sequence 0 → Sel_T(gr_2 U) → Sel_T(U⟨2⟩) → Sel_T(U⟨1⟩) is exact in the torsor sense (NC.3/central-selmer-dimension), so dim Sel_T(U⟨2⟩) ≤ dim Sel_T(H₁) + dim Sel_T(Q_p(1)).

Sel_T(Q_p(1)) = Z^× ⊗ Q_p = 0 (SIC L0/s-unit-kummer-identification). Sel_T(H₁) = H¹_f(G_Q, V_pE): at ℓ ≠ p the local H¹ of V_pE vanishes for potentially good reduction (weights), and at p potentially crystalline classes are de Rham, where H¹_g = H¹_f for V_pE; it has dimension one by hypothesis (SIC L4/elliptic-finite-kummer).
On the de Rham side F⁰(gr_2 U_dR) = 0 because F⁰H₁ ∧ F⁰H₁ = 0, so dim U_dR⟨2⟩/F⁰ = 3 − 1 = 2.
The refined conditions are finer than Kim's, so NC.4/locus-compatibilities and NC.4/dimension-finiteness give finiteness.
acceptance: The congruent-number curve y² = x³ − 25x has CM by Z[i] and E(Q) of rank one, generated modulo torsion by (−4, 6); with Ш(E)[p^∞] finite it satisfies the hypothesis.
The depth used is 2 in this roadmap's indexing (Kim's U_3).

sources.match: Defines the potentially unramified and potentially crystalline refined Selmer varieties, proves the central exact sequence for them and computes the depth-two dimensions for a rank-one CM curve, obtaining finiteness of integral points independently of conjectures.

nodes.title: Pseudo-nullity implies the dimension conjecture for punctured CM curves
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have complex multiplication, X = E ∖ {O}, p an odd prime of good reduction, F_1 = Q(E[p]), F_∞ = Q(E[p^∞]), G_∞ = Gal(F_∞/F_1), Λ = Z_p[[G_∞]] (for p odd of good reduction, p is unramified in the CM field K, K ⊆ F_1 and G_∞ is open in 1 + p(O_K ⊗ Z_p) ≅ Z_p², so Λ ≅ Z_p[[T_1, T_2]] is a regular local domain), and I the Galois group of the maximal abelian unramified pro-p extension of F_∞ in which the primes above T split completely. Assume the Coates–Sujatha conjecture that I, a finitely generated Λ-module, is pseudo-null. Then KimDimensionConjecture holds for X (working over F_1, which suffices because corestriction is surjective on H²), and hence 𝒳(Z) is finite.
hypotheses: The pseudo-nullity of the finitely generated Λ-module I is a hypothesis; p is odd, so that G_∞ is torsion-free of rank two and Λ is the integrally closed domain of PMIA L4/pseudo-null.
The H² estimate is reduced to F_1; local terms are bounded as in h2-growth-bound with g = 1.
proofSteps: It suffices to bound dim H²(G_T, H₁^{⊗n}) by a polynomial in n; the local contributions are bounded as in NC.6/h2-growth-bound, so it suffices to bound Ш²_T(H₁^{⊗n}).

By Poitou–Tate this is dual to Sel⁰_T(H¹^{⊗n}(1)). The Hochschild–Serre sequence for F_∞/F_1 in continuous cohomology of the inverse system H¹(Ē, Z/p^i)^{⊗n}(1) (Jannsen; requested from D7) identifies it, after inverting p, with Hom_Λ(I, H¹^{⊗n}(1)): the terms H^j(G_∞, H¹^{⊗n}(1)) ⊗ Q vanish for j = 1, 2 and n ≠ 2, because G_∞ contains homotheties u ∈ 1 + p^r Z_p of T_pE (the CM image is open in (O_K ⊗ Z_p)^×), which are central and act on H¹^{⊗n}(1) by the scalar u^{2−n} ≠ 1.

Pseudo-nullity makes I ⊗ Q_p finite-dimensional: the Z_p-torsion of I maps to zero in every Q_p-vector space, and I′ = I/I[p^∞] is pseudo-null with p a nonzerodivisor, so dim I′/pI′ ≤ 0, I′/pI′ is finite, and I′ is finitely generated over Z_p by Nakayama's lemma for compact modules. (Kim asserts finite generation of I itself over Z_p, citing Greenberg 1978; that fails for p-torsion pseudo-null modules such as Λ/(p, T_1): source issue E-NC6-kim-pseudonull-fg.) A Frobenius element of G_∞ therefore has finitely many eigenvalues on I ⊗ Q_p, and by weights Hom_Λ(I, H¹^{⊗n}(1)) = 0 for n ≫ 0.
Conclude as in vanishing-implies-dimension with the polynomial bound.
acceptance: The hypothesis is about F_∞ = Q(E[p^∞]), a two-dimensional p-adic Lie extension of F_1 in the CM case.
With g = 1 the local bound is polynomial in n, and d_n ~ 2^n/n for m = 2.

sources.match: Derives Conjecture 1 for a punctured CM curve from the pseudo-nullity conjecture of Coates and Sujatha through Poitou–Tate, Hochschild–Serre and a weight argument; the finite-generation claim on p.131 is replaced by the weaker statement the weight argument uses (source issue E-NC6-kim-pseudonull-fg).

nodes.title: The dimension conjecture for the thrice-punctured line
nodes.statement: Let X = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z[1/S] with S a finite set of primes, b ∈ 𝒳(Z[1/S]) an S-integral base point (if 𝒳(Z[1/S]) is empty there is nothing to prove), and p ∉ S an odd prime. Then KimDimensionConjecture(X, p) holds, hence X(Z[1/S]) is finite (Siegel's theorem for this curve). Explicitly gr_n U ≅ Q_p(n)^{r_n} with r_n the Witt numbers for m = 2, F⁰ = 0 on U_dR so dim Q_n = Σ_{k ≤ n} r_k, and dim S_n ≤ |S|·2 + Σ_{3 ≤ k ≤ n, k odd} r_k, which is smaller for n large.
hypotheses: S finite, p ∉ S odd (the supplier request to ArithmeticKTheory N.5 is for odd p); T = S ∪ {p}; the base point is S-integral, as in Kim 2005 p.17.
Uses Soulé's computation of H¹(G_T, Q_p(k)): zero for even k ≥ 2 and one-dimensional for odd k ≥ 3.
Kim 2005 also takes p large compared with the depth for its comparison maps; here the comparison is that of NC.4, for every prime of good reduction.
proofSteps: H₁ = Q_p(1)² and gr_n U is a quotient of H₁^{⊗n}, so gr_n U ≅ Q_p(n)^{r_n} with r_n from NC.6/graded-central-dimensions.
H¹_f(G_T, Q_p(1)) = Z[1/S]^× ⊗ Q_p has dimension |S| (SIC L0/s-unit-kummer-identification); H¹(G_T, Q_p(k)) = 0 for even k ≥ 2 and has dimension one for odd k ≥ 3 (Soulé; ArithmeticKTheory N.5).
The central-extension fibration gives dim S_n ≤ 2|S| + Σ_{odd 3 ≤ k ≤ n} r_k (NC.3/central-extension).
Since the Hodge filtration of H¹_dR is F¹ = everything, F⁰U_dR is trivial and dim Q_n = Σ_{k ≤ n} r_k; the even-degree terms make the difference positive for large n.
Finiteness follows from NC.4/dimension-finiteness.
acceptance: S = ∅: 𝒳(Z) is empty, and the depth-one dimensions, which need no base point, are dim H¹_f(G_T, Q_p(1)²) = 0 < 2 = dim Q_1.
S = {2}: depth 1 gives 2 = 2, depth 2 gives 2 < 3, in agreement with BDCKW §8.2.

sources.locator: Introduction, pp.1–2; §3, proof of the main theorem, pp.17–18
sources.match: Chooses an S-integral base point when one exists (p.17), bounds the Selmer dimension using the Tate-twist graded pieces and Soulé's vanishing, compares with the de Rham dimension and deduces Siegel's theorem for the thrice-punctured line; the index range printed on p.18 needs the correction in sourceIssues.
Records that Conjecture 1 is proved in genus zero.

nodes.title: Kim's conjecture on eventual equality
nodes.statement: Let 𝒳 → Spec Z be a regular minimal model of a hyperbolic curve over Q in one of the three cases of BDCKW §2.1 (P¹ minus a reduced horizontal divisor with at least three geometric points; the regular minimal model of a smooth proper curve of genus ≥ 2; or the complement of a nonempty reduced horizontal divisor in the regular minimal model of a smooth proper curve of genus ≥ 1), b an integral point or integral tangent vector, p an odd prime of good reduction and T a finite set of primes containing p and the bad primes. Let U⟨n⟩ be the depth-n quotient of the Q_p-unipotent étale fundamental group (BDCKW's U_n), j_v: 𝒳(Z_v) → H¹(G_v, U⟨n⟩) the local unipotent Kummer maps, and Sel_n(𝒳) = ⋂_{v ≠ p} loc_v⁻¹(Im j_v) ⊆ H¹_f(G_T, U⟨n⟩), with the scheme structure given by the sum of the ideals (each Im j_v is finite and is the base point for v ∉ T). Put X(Z_p)_n = j_p⁻¹(loc_p(Sel_n(𝒳))) ⊆ 𝒳(Z_p). These sets decrease with n, contain 𝒳(Z), and do not depend on T or b. The proposition KimConjecture(𝒳, p) states that X(Z_p)_n = 𝒳(Z) for all sufficiently large n (BDCKW Conjecture 3.1). For a finite set S of primes with p ∉ S, dropping the conditions at v ∈ S gives Sel_{n,S}(𝒳), X(Z_p)_{S,n} ⊇ 𝒳(Z[1/S]), and the S-integral proposition KimConjecture_S(𝒳, p): X(Z_p)_{S,n} = 𝒳(Z[1/S]) for n large (BDCKW §8.1). Both are open and are stated as named propositions; BDCKW do not formulate a version over other number fields (§3.2), and none is stated here.
hypotheses: 𝒳 a regular minimal Z-model as in BDCKW §2.1; p odd of good reduction for 𝒳 and b.
In NC.4 terms, X(Z_p)_n is the crystalline locus crystallineLocus_n for the stringent local conditions C_v = Im j_v at v ≠ p and the crystalline condition at p.
Depth indexing: U⟨n⟩ = U/Γ_{n+1}U, so n = 1 is the abelian depth.

When b is an integral tangent vector (as for P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z, which has no integral point), the Selmer scheme, the local Kummer maps and the loci use NC.2–NC.4 at the tangential fibre functor: recorded gap on tangential base points.
proofSteps: Represent H¹_f(G_T, U⟨n⟩) and the localisation maps (NC.3/selmer-functor, NC.3/selmer-representability).
Finiteness of Im j_v for v ≠ p (Kim–Tamagawa, as cited by BDCKW 2.5) and triviality for good v ∉ T make Sel_n(𝒳) a closed subscheme; define X(Z_p)_n through the local Kummer map j_p (NC.4/kim-loci).
Monotonicity in n and containment of 𝒳(Z) follow from NC.4/locus-compatibilities and NC.4/rational-integral-containment.
Independence of T and b: BDCKW §2.8 (inflation lemma for closed normal subgroups) and §2.9 (twisting by the path torsor P(b, c)).
Define the propositions as eventual equality.
acceptance: For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z and p = 5, X(Z_5)_1 = ∅ = 𝒳(Z) (NC.6/thrice-punctured-depth-one).
For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z and p = 7, X(Z_7)_1 consists of the two primitive sixth roots of unity, so equality fails at depth 1.

sources.match: Defines the Selmer scheme with stringent local conditions, the nested loci and their independence of T and the base point, states the eventual equality conjecture over Z, notes that no number-field version is formulated, and introduces the S-integral variant.

uses.how: The conjecture is tested by computing X(Z_p)_n for punctured elliptic curves, the thrice-punctured line and Fermat curves.
Presented as the unipotent counterpart of the surjectivity in the section conjecture and of finiteness of Ш.
The depth-one instance proved in BDCKW §6.1.
Certified enumeration compares a computed finite locus with the known global points; equality at some depth is what makes such a comparison exhaustive.

api.name: kimLocus
api.statement: X(Z_p)_n = j_p⁻¹(loc_p(Sel_n(𝒳))) ⊆ 𝒳(Z_p).

api.name: kimLocus_antitone
api.statement: X(Z_p)_{n+1} ⊆ X(Z_p)_n for every n ≥ 1.

api.name: integral_subset_kimLocus
api.statement: 𝒳(Z) ⊆ X(Z_p)_n for every n.

api.name: kimConjecture_iff_exists_subset
api.statement: KimConjecture(𝒳, p) holds if and only if X(Z_p)_n ⊆ 𝒳(Z) for some n, by the two previous items.

api.name: kimLocus_eq_crystallineLocus
api.statement: X(Z_p)_n equals NC.4's crystallineLocus_n for the stringent local conditions.

api.name: kimLocus_indep_T
api.statement: For T ⊆ T′ both containing p and the bad primes, the Selmer schemes for T and T′ are isomorphic compatibly with loc_p, so X(Z_p)_n does not depend on T.

api.statement: Twisting by the path torsor P(b, c) identifies the Selmer schemes for integral base points b and c compatibly with loc_p and the Kummer maps, so X(Z_p)_n does not depend on b.

api.name: kimConjectureS
api.statement: The S-integral proposition: X(Z_p)_{S,n} = 𝒳(Z[1/S]) for n large, with KimConjectureS ∅ = KimConjecture.

api.name: EventualEquality
api.statement: The form on families of sets: L n = G for all large n; KimConjecture is the instance L n = X(Z_p)_n, G = 𝒳(Z).

api.name: eventualEquality_iff_exists_subset
api.statement: For an antitone family L with G ⊆ L n for all n, eventual equality holds if and only if L n ⊆ G for some n.

api.name: eventualEquality_iInter

tests.name: kimConjecture_thrice_punctured_p5
tests.statement: For 𝒳 = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z with the tangential base point at 0 and p = 5, X(Z_5)_1 = ∅ = 𝒳(Z), so the conjecture holds from depth 1 (BDCKW §6.1).

tests.name: kimLocus_thrice_punctured_p7
tests.statement: For the same 𝒳 and p = 7, X(Z_7)_1 = {ζ_6, ζ_6⁵} ≠ 𝒳(Z) = ∅: equality is eventual, not at depth 1 (BDCKW §6.2).

tests.name: kimConjecture_not_intersection
tests.statement: Eventual equality is stronger than ⋂_n X(Z_p)_n = 𝒳(Z): for the decreasing family L_n = G ∪ {m ∈ ℕ : m ≥ n} with G finite, the intersection is G but no L_n equals G, so a definition by the intersection would accept it.

tests.name: kimConjectureS_empty
tests.statement: For S = ∅ the S-integral Selmer scheme is Sel_n(𝒳) and KimConjectureS reduces to KimConjecture.

tests.name: kimLocusS_half_contains
tests.statement: For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z[1/2] and an odd prime p, the three points 2, −1 and 1/2 lie in X(Z_p)_{{2},2}, the zero set of 2Li_2(z) + log(z)log(1 − z) (BDCKW §8.2).

nodes.title: Kim's conjecture at depth one for the thrice-punctured line
nodes.statement: Let 𝒳 = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z with the tangential base point at 0. Then 𝒳(Z) = ∅. At depth 1, U⟨1⟩ = Q_p(1)², Sel_1(𝒳) = 0 and j_p(z) = (log z, log(1 − z)), so X(Z_p)_1 is the set of z ∈ Z_p with z and 1 − z both roots of unity, which is the set of primitive sixth roots of unity lying in Z_p. Hence for p = 3 or p ≡ 2 mod 3, X(Z_p)_1 = ∅ and KimConjecture(𝒳, p) holds from depth 1. For p ≡ 1 mod 3, X(Z_p)_1 = {ζ_6, ζ_6⁵}; Sel_2(𝒳) = 0 by Soulé's vanishing H¹(G_T, Q_p(2)) = 0, and X(Z_p)_2 = ∅ if and only if the p-adic dilogarithm Li_2(ζ_6) is nonzero. BDCKW report that Li_2(ζ_6) ≠ 0 for 3 ≤ p < 10⁵ by a numerical computation; that report is not a theorem of this layer.
hypotheses: p odd; 𝒳(Z) = ∅ because z and 1 − z cannot both be units of Z.
The depth-two statement for p ≡ 1 mod 3 is an equivalence with a nonvanishing condition, not an unconditional equality.
The tangential base point at 0 uses the recorded gap on tangential base points.
proofSteps: 𝒳(Z) is empty: the only units are ±1, and 1 − 1 = 0, 1 − (−1) = 2.
Sel_1(𝒳) = 0: it is (Z^× ⊗ Q_p)² with the stringent conditions (NC.3/depth-one-selmer-comparison, SIC L0/s-unit-kummer-identification).

The local Kummer map at the tangential base point has as coordinates the regularised iterated integrals from 0 (NC.4/iterated-coordinates, at the tangential base point: recorded gap): ∫dz/z = log z and ∫dz/(z − 1) = log(1 − z) at depth 1, and the depth-2 coordinate −Li_2(z) (ColemanIntegration L1/punctured-line-coleman-functions). A zero of the p-adic logarithm on Z_p^× is a root of unity, and z, 1 − z both roots of unity forces z to be a primitive sixth root of unity.
A primitive sixth root of unity lies in Z_p exactly when p ≡ 1 mod 3.

For p ≡ 1 mod 3, Sel_2(𝒳) = 0 because H¹(G_T, Q_p(2)) = 0, so X(Z_p)_2 is cut out by the depth-2 coordinate −Li_2(z) as well; since Li_2(ζ_6⁻¹) = −Li_2(ζ_6) (ColemanIntegration L2/inversion-relation with log ζ_6 = 0), the two candidates vanish or survive together.
acceptance: p = 7: X(Z_7)_1 = {3, 5} modulo the identification of ζ_6 with the Teichmüller lifts of 3 and 5, the primitive sixth roots of unity mod 7.

sources.match: Computes the depth-one locus of the thrice-punctured line through the logarithms, proves the depth-one case for p = 3 and p ≡ 2 mod 3, reduces the depth-two case for p ≡ 1 mod 3 to nonvanishing of Li_2 at a sixth root of unity, and reports the numerical check.

Künneth for ℓ-adic and p-adic étale cohomology of a product of smooth varieties over a field of characteristic zero, Galois-equivariantly and compatibly with Tate twists: for smooth curves, H¹(C_{F̄})^{⊗n} is a Galois-stable direct summand of H^n(C^n_{F̄}); for a smooth projective V′ over a finite extension F′/F, the induced representation Ind H^i(V′_{F̄}) is a direct summand of H^i of the Weil restriction Res_{F′/F}V′.

The Hochschild–Serre exact sequence 0 → H¹(G/N, M^N) → H¹(G, M) → H⁰(G/N, H¹(N, M)) → H²(G/N, M^N) in continuous cohomology of profinite groups with coefficients an inverse system of finite modules satisfying the Mittag-Leffler condition (Jannsen), and its rational version.

For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve X′ over a field F of characteristic zero, a finite étale divisor D ⊂ X′ with complement X and a prime p: the G_F-equivariant Gysin (localization) exact sequence 0 → H¹(X′_{F̄}, Q_p) → H¹(X_{F̄}, Q_p) → ker(Q_p(−1)^{D(F̄)} → Q_p(−1)) → 0, obtained from purity i^!Q_p ≅ Q_p(−1)[−2] at the points of D with the trace map as the last arrow, and dually 0 → coker(Q_p(1) → Q_p(1)^{D(F̄)}) → H₁(X_{F̄}, Q_p) → H₁(X′_{F̄}, Q_p) → 0.

gaps.title: Primary source for Labute's dimension formula not read
gaps.detail: The surface-group case of graded-central-dimensions (Σ_{k|n} k·d_k = α^n + β^n) is taken from Kim 2009 pp.122–123, which cites Labute, J. Algebra 14 (1970), 16–23. The publisher did not serve that paper to this worker. The formula was checked against the free survey of Linton and Nyberg-Brodda (arXiv:2501.18306, §1.7.6, equation (32), p.62), which gives it in genus 2 and the growth rate g + √(g² − 1) in every genus, and against small cases (g = 1 gives the abelian case; g = 2 gives d_2 = 5 = dim Λ²H₁ − 1 and d_3 = 16). It is also equivalent to the enveloping algebra of the graded Lie algebra having Hilbert series 1/(1 − 2g t + t²) (take logarithms of the PBW product). A follow-up reads Labute 1970 or Labute, Invent. Math. 4 (1967), Théorème 2, and pins the primary locator for all g.

gaps.title: Bloch–Kato Conjecture 5.3 read only through Kim
gaps.detail: Bloch–Kato, 'L-functions and Tamagawa numbers of motives' (Grothendieck Festschrift I, 1990) is not freely available to this worker. sourceIssues.locator: Publ. RIMS 45 (2009), §3, proof of Proposition 2, p.123 (published version).
sourceIssues.printed: For n odd, the right-hand side of the Euler characteristic formula, the dimension of the (−1)-eigenspace of complex conjugation on the graded piece Z_{n+1}\Z_n, is asserted to be d_n/2, by comparison with complex Hodge theory.
sourceIssues.correction: The value d_n/2 holds when the graded piece is pure of odd weight, which is the compact case. In general the (−1)-eigenspace has dimension (d_n − τ_n)/2, where τ_n is the trace of complex conjugation on the graded piece, computed from its trace t on H₁ by τ_n = (1/n)Σ_{e|n} μ(e) t_e^{n/e} (t_e = t for odd e, t_e = m for even e). Either |t| < m and τ_n = o(d_n), or t = −m and conjugation acts by (−1)^n; in both cases the sum of the (+1)-eigenspace dimensions still grows like λ^n/n with λ > g, so Proposition 2 survives with this replacement.
sourceIssues.reason: For X = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Q, each graded piece is Q_p(n)^{d_n} and complex conjugation acts on Q_p(n) by (−1)^n, so for odd n the (−1)-eigenspace is the whole piece, of dimension d_n, not d_n/2. In the affine case the graded pieces are mixed (the boundary contributes Tate twists of even weight), and the Hodge-symmetry argument applies only to pure odd weight.
